question: Should OpenClaw bundle and maintain the Vault SecretRef exec provider, or keep Vault outside core on the existing plugin integration seam?
rationale: The code path looks plausible and covered, but this is an ownership and security-boundary choice because it adds a credential-bearing network resolver, Vault auth environment pass-through, plugin enablement behavior, and dependency metadata to the bundled distribution.

options.title: Bundle after security approval
options.body: Approve the bundled Vault plugin once maintainers accept the exec resolver trust model, dependency metadata, and operator support surface.

options.title: Keep Vault external
options.body: Pause or close the PR and direct Vault to an external or ClawHub plugin because the current SecretRef provider seam already supports it.

options.title: Hold for hardening sponsor
options.body: Keep the PR open but require a named maintainer/security owner to define additional hardening or dependency conditions before merge.

recommendation.title: Bundle after security approval
recommendation.body: Approve the bundled Vault plugin once maintainers accept the exec resolver trust model, dependency metadata, and operator support surface.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is closest to the recent SecretRef security/runtime hardening boundary rather than a mechanical plugin implementation issue.
